la:adv:adhuc.gloss: so far, thus far, hitherto, still, yet
senses: so far, thus far, hitherto, still, yet
again; furthermore; moreover; besides (used in scholastic debates to introduce an additional point in one's argument)
la:adv:adhuc.html:
ăd-huc, adv.
Prop., of place, to this place, hitherto, thus far (designating the limit, inclusive of the whole space traversed: hence often joined with usque; cf. ad, A. 1. B.): conveniunt adhuc utriusque verba,thus far, to this point, the statements of both agree,: adhuc ea dixi, causa cur Zenoni non fuisset,; cf. : his oris, quas angulo Baeticae adhuc usque perstrinximus,.—Hence, in the desig. of measure or degree, so far, to such a degree: et ipse Caesar erat adhuc impudens, qui exercitum et provinciam invito senatu teneret,; so ; ; .—More frequently,
Transf.
Of time, until now, hitherto, as yet (designating the limit, together with the period already passed; cf. ad, 1. B.): res adhuc quidem hercle in tuto est,: celabitur itidem ut celata adhuc est,: sicut adhuc fecerunt, speculabuntur,: ille vidit non modo, quot fuissent adhuc philosophorum de summo bono, sed quot omnino esse possent sententiae,: haec adhuc (sc. acta sunt): sed ad praeterita revertamur,; so ; ; : Britanni, qui adhuc pugnae expertes,; so —With usque or semper: usque adhuc actum est probe,; so ; ; ; ; ; : quod adhuc semper tacui et tacendum putavi,.—With dum in subordinate propositions, for the purpose of more accurate desig. of time: quae adhuc te carens, dum hic fui, sustentabam,what I have endured during the whole time that I have been here, until now,: adhuc dum mihi nullo loco deesse vis, numquam te confirmare potuisti,; so .—Hence the adverbial expression (occurring once in Plautus): adhuc locorum, until now, hitherto: ut adhuc locorum feci, faciam sedulo, Capt. 2, 3, 25.— Adhuc denotes not merely a limitation of time in the present, but also, though more rarely, like usque eo and ad id tempus, and the Engl. as yet, in the past: adhuc haec erant, ad reliqua alacri tendebamus animo,: Abraham vero adhuc stabat,: unam adhuc a te epistulam acceperam,: cum adhuc sustinuisset multos dies,: scripsi etiam illud quodam in libello ... disertos me cognōsse nonnullos, eloquentem adhuc neminem,: una adhuc victoria Carus Metius censebatur,.—
Adhuc non, or neque adhuc, not as yet, not to this time: nihil adhuc, nothing as yet, or not at all as yet: numquam adhuc, never as yet, never yet: cupidissimi veniendi maximis injuriis affecti, adhuc non venerunt,: me adhuc non legisse turpe utrique nostrum est,; so ; ; ; : cui neque fulgor adhuc nec dum sua forma recessit,: nihil adhuc peccavit etiam,: nihil adhuc est, quod vereare,: sed quod quaeris, quando, qua, quo, nihil adhuc scimus,; so 9, 17, 7; ; : numquam etiam quicquam adhuc verborum est prolocutus perperam,; cf. .—
For etiam nunc, yet, still; to denote continuance (apparently not used by Cic.): stertis adhuc?are you still snoring?; adhuc tranquilla res est,it is still quiet,; so : Ephesi regem est consecutus fluctuantem adhuc animo,; so 21, 43, 14; ; ; ; ; ; ; : quinque satis fuerant; nam sex septemve libelli est nimium: quid adhuc ludere, Musa, juvat? why play still, still more, or further? ; so .—
Hence also to denote that a thing is still remaining or existing: at in veterum comicorum adhuc libris invenio,I yet find in the old comic poets,: quippe tres adhuc legiones erant,were still left,; so ; ; .—With vb. omitted: si quis adhuc precibus locus, exue mentem,.—
To denote that a thing has only reached a certain point, now first, just now: cum adhuc (now for the first time) naso odos obsecutus es meo, da vicissim meo gutturi gaudium, : gangraenam vero, si nondum plane tenet, sed adhuc incipit, curare non difficillimum est,; so .—Hence, with deinde or aliquando following: quam concedis adhuc artem omnino non esse, sed aliquando,: senatus priusquam edicto convocaretur ad curiam concurrit, obseratisque adhuc foribus, deinde apertis, tantas mortuo gratias agit, etc.,; so .—
To denote that a thing had reached a certain limit before another thing happened (in prose only after Livy), still, yet, while yet: inconditam multitudinem adhuc disjecit,he dispersed the multitude while yet unarranged,.—
For etiam, insuper, praeterea, to denote that a thing occurs beside or along with another (belonging perhaps only to popular language, hence once in Plaut., and to the post-Aug. per.), besides, further, moreover: addam minam adhuc istic postea,: unam rem adhuc adiciam,: sunt adhuc aliquae non omittendae in auro differentiae,; so ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; .—
In later Lat. adhuc is used like etiam in the Cic. per., = ἔτι, yet, still, for the sake of emphasis in comparisons; then, if it enhances the comparative, it stands before it; but follows it, if that which the comp. expresses is added by way of augmentation; as, he has done a still greater thing, and he has still done a greater thing (this is the view of Hand, Turs. I. p. 166): tum Callicles adhuc concitatior,: adhuc difficilior observatio est per tenores,: si marmor illi (Phidiae), si adhuc viliorem materiem obtulisses, fecisset, etc.,: adhuc diligentius,: cui gloriae amplior

adhuc ex opportunitate cumulus accessit, : Di faveant, majora adhuc restant,; so ; ; .

Adhuc sometimes = adeo, even (in the connection, et adhuc, -que adhuc; v. adeo, II.).
Ita res successit meliusque adhuc, : Tellurem Nymphasque et adhuc ignota precatur flumina,: Nil parvum sapias et adhuc sublimia cures,; so ; ; .—
Absol.: gens non astuta nec callida aperit adhuc secreta pectoris licentiā joci,: cetera similes Batavis, nisi quod ipso adhuc terrae suae solo et caelo acrius animantur, (cf.: ipse adeo under adeo, II., and at the end); so .—See more upon this word, Hand, Turs. I. pp. 156-167.

la:verb:adhibeo.html:
ăd-hĭbĕo, ŭi, ĭtum, 2, v. a.
habeo
,
to hold toward or to, to turn, bring, add to; with ad, in, dat. or absol.
In gen.
Lit.: cur non adhibuisti, dum istaec loquereris, tympanum,: huc adhibete aurīs (ad ea) quae ego loquar,: ad mea formosos vultus adhibete carmina,; cf. : manus medicas ad vulnera,: odores ad deos,: quos negat ad panem adhibere quidquam, praeter nasturtium,to eat with it,: alicui calcaria, (cf. addere calcar, v. addo): manus genibus adhibet, i. e. admovet, genua amplexatur,: vincula captis,to put them on them,.—
Trop.: metum ut mihi adhibeam,; cf. : nunc animum nobis adhibe veram ad rationem,; : vacuas aurīs adhibe ad veram rationem,; cf. ; : ut oratio, quae lumen adhibere rebus debet, ea obscuritatem afferat,: est ea (oratio) quidem utilior, sed raro proficit neque est ad vulgus adhibenda,: adhibere cultus, honores, preces, diis immortalibus,; cf. : alicui voluptates,: consolationem,: omnes ii motus, quos orator adhibere volet judici,which the orator may wish to communicate to the judge,—Hence = addere, adjungere, to add to: uti quattuor initiis rerum illis quintam hanc naturam non adhiberet,: ad domesticorum majorumque morem etiam hanc a Socrate adventitiam doctrinam adhibuerunt,.
Esp.
Of persons, to bring one to a place, to summon, to employ (cf. the Engl. to have one up): hoc temere numquam amittam ego a me, quin mihi testes adhibeam,; so ; : medicum,: leges, ad quas (sc. defendendas) adhibemur,we are summoned,: nec, quoniam apud Graecos judices res agetur, poteris adhibere Demosthenem,: adhibebitur heros,shall be brought upon the stage,: castris adhibere socios et foedera jungere,: aliquem in partem periculi,: in auxilium,.—
Adhibere ad or in consilium, to send for one in order to receive counsel from him, to consult one: neque hos ad concilium adhibendos censeo,: in consilium,; so also absol.: a tuis reliquis non adhibemur,we are not consulted,; so ; ,

7; ; ; ; ; cf. Cortius ad , and ad .—But sometimes adhibere in consilium = admittere in cons., to admit to a consultation. —So trop.: est tuum, sic agitare animo, ut non adhibeas in consilium cogitationum tuarum desperationem aut timorem,.—

Adhibere aliquem cenae, epulis, etc., to invite to a dinner, to a banquet, etc., to entertain: adhibete Penatīs et patrios epulis, etc.,; so ; ; : in convivium, Nep. praef. 7.—And absol., to receive, to treat: quos ego universos adhiberi liberaliter dico oportere,: Quintum filium severius adhibebo,.—
Adhibere se ad aliquid, to betake or apply one's self to a thing, i. e. to devote attention to it: adhibere se remotum a curis veram ad rationem, (cf. above I. A.); and absol.: adhibere se, to appear or to behave one's self in any manner: permagni est hominis, sic se adhibere in tanta potestate, ut nulla alia potestas ab iis, quibus ipse praeest, desideretur,.—
Adhibere aliquid ad aliquid, alicui rei, or with in and abl., to put a thing to a determinate use, to apply, to use or employ for or in any thing definite (therefore, with intention and deliberation; on the contr., usurpare denotes merely momentary use; cf. ; and uti, use that arises from some necessity, Herz. ad ): adhibere omnem diligentiam ad convalescendum,; cf. ; : cautionem privatis rebus suis,: medicinam aegroto,: humatis titulum, i. e. inscriptionem addere,: belli necessitatibus patientiam,: fraudem testamento,: curam viis,: fidem et diligentiam in amicorum periculis,: misericordiam in fortunis alicujus et sapientiam in salute reip.,: flores in causis,: curam in valetudine tuenda,; and with de: curam de aliqua re,: modum, to set a limit to, to set bounds to: vitio,: sumptibus,: cf. ; : voluptati,: memoriam contumeliae,to retain it in memory,.—
Adhibere aliquid, in gen., to use, employ, exercise: neque quisquam parsimoniam adhibet,: fidem,: celeritatem,: calumniam, fraudem, dolum, id. Auct. Or. pro Dom. 14, 36: modum quemdam,; : nulla arte adhibita,: sollertiam, Tibull. 3, 4, 75: querelas,: adhibere moram = differre,.—
In later Lat.: alicui aliquem, to bring up, quote one to another as authority for an assertion: is nos aquam multam ex diluta nive bibentis coërcebat, severiusque increpabat adhibebatque nobis auctoritates nobilium medicorum,.

senses: to be close to (a person or thing), be near to, hang on, keep close to
to trail, drag after; to be the last
la:verb:adhaereo.html:
ăd-haerĕo, haesi, haesum, 2, v. n.,
to cleave or stick to a thing.
Lit., of iron adhering to a magnet: unus ubi ex uno dependet, subter adhaerens,; cf. : tota adhaerens (lingua) crocodilis, cleaving to his palate, .—With in and abl.: tela in tuis visceribus,; so .—With acc.: cratera et corvus adhaeret, (so Tert.: humerum, de ).—With abl.: fronte cuspis,.—With dat., poet.: tonsis (ovibus) illotus sudor,: veteri craterae limus adhaesit,; and in later prose: navis ancoris,is fastened to them,: stativis castris,; and: jumento,to stick to,.—
Fig.
In gen., to cling to, adhere to: adhaesit homini ad intimum ventrem fames,; and of fawning adherence to one,: cui canis ex vero dictum cognomen adhaeret,adheres,: nulli fortunae adhaerebat animus, i. e. inconstans fuit,: obsidioni fortiter adhaerentes,.—
Adhaerere alicui, to be close to a person or thing, to be near, to hang on, keep close to, etc. (mostly post-Cic., esp. in the histt.): vineis modica silva adhaerebat,was close to it, adjoined it,; so .—Of persons: procul abesse Romanos: lateri adhaerere gravem dominum, i. e. he (the King of Macedon) hangs on them, threatens them by his nearness, : nec umquam non adhaerentes,and never departing from his side,: comitem perpetuo alicui adhaerere,: tempus adhaerens,the time in hand, just the present time,: obvio quoque adhaerente,while each one adhered to him,; and so trop.: adhaeret altissimis invidia,.—
To hang on a thing, i. e. to trail or drag after, to be the last, sarcastically in Cic.: tenesne memoriā te extremum adhaesisse? hung on the end, i. e. extremo loco quaestorem esse factum, Vat. 5 (cf. haerere, , and Gron. ad h. l.); and without sarcasm,.

senses: alternative form of adhaerēns (“cleaving or sticking to”)

la:verb:adheresco.gloss: to adhere tightly; to stick fast

la:verb:adhortor.gloss: to encourage, rouse, stimulate, rally, urge or exhort someone to something
senses: to encourage, rouse, stimulate, rally, urge or exhort someone to something
la:verb:adhortor.html:
ăd-hortor, āri, ātus, 1, v. dep.,
to encourage, urge, exhort one to a thing, constr. with ad, in, de, or absol.: nam me meae vitae consuetudo ad C. Rabirium defendendum est adhortata,: ne posset aliquando ad bellum faciendum locus ipse adhortari,: aliquem ad certam laudem,: loricatos ad discumbendum,: in bellum,: in ultionem sui,: de re frumentaria Boios atque Aeduos adhortari non destitit,he did not cease to incite and spur on the Boii and Aedui, in respect to a supply of corn,.—Absol.: milites,: nullo adhortante sibi quisque dux et instigator,.—Followed by ut, ne, or the simple subj.: adhort. adulescentes, ut turbulenti velint esse,: tandem Bruto adhortante, ne jamdudum operientes destitueret,: adhortor, properent,: adhortari se, to rouse or bestir one's self: ferus ipse (leo) sese adhortans rapidum incitat animo, Catull. 63, 85.!*? Pass.: adulati erant ab amicis et adhortati, Cassius ap. P.: punctione aliqua adhortati vel titillati, Cael. Aurel. Acut. 2, 3.

la:verb:adhaeresco.gloss: to adhere tightly; to stick fast
senses: to adhere tightly; to stick fast
la:verb:adhaeresco.html:
ăd-haeresco, haesi, haesum, 3,
v. inch. [adhaereo], to cleave or stick to, to adhere, lit. and trop. (in the trop. sense almost exclusively belonging to Cic.).
Lit., constr. with ad, in, and abl. or ubi: tragula ad turrim,: ne quid emineret, ubi ignis adhaeresceret,: tamquam in quodam incili, Cael. ap. : si potes in his locis adhaerescere, if you can stick (i. e. stay or sojourn) in such places, : in me omnia conjurationis nefaria tela adhaeserunt, Auct. Or. pro Dom. 24; cf. ; ad quamcunque disciplinam, tamquam ad saxum, adhaerescunt,: argumentum ratio ipsa confirmat, quae simul atque emissa est, adhaerescit, sc. ad mentem,sticks fast to, is fastened upon the memory (the figure is derived from missiles), .—With dat.: justitiae honestatique, to be attached or devoted to, .—And absol.: oratio ita libere fluebat, ut numquam adhaeresceret,never was at a stand, faltered,; cf. (v. haereo): adhaerescere ad columnam (sc. Maeniam); sarcastically, to remain fixed at the debtor's columns, i. e. to be punished as a fraudulent debtor, ; cf. .—
Fig., to correspond to, to accord with, to fit to or suit: si non omnia, quae praeponerentur a me ad omnium vestrūm studium, adhaerescerent,.

la:noun:adhaesio.html:
ădhaesĭo, ōnis, f.
adhaereo
,
an adhering, adhesion: complexiones et copulationes et adhaesiones atomorum inter se,, v. Madv. ad h. l.; Gloss. Mai.

senses: An exhortation intended to win the consent or desire of the audience.
la:noun:adhortatio.html:
ădhortātĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
,
an exhortation,encouragement (class.): omissa nostra adhortatione veniamus ad eorum sermonem, * : cum clamore comprobata adhortatio esset,; ; ; ; ;
